student_passage:
When I returned to the club room after helping outside, only one grey coat was hanging beside the door. It looked like mine, except that its top button was made of wood. Mine had a blue plastic button, or at least I thought it did. The room was empty, so there was nobody to ask. (1) ____ That plan lasted only until I heard the rain against the windows. I needed to get home before it became heavier.

I checked the coat again, looking for something that a stranger would be unlikely to have. At first I found only an ordinary paper tissue. Then my fingers touched a rough edge hidden deeper in the lining. (2) ____ I remembered sewing it there during a lesson after I had torn the pocket on a fence. The stitches were untidy in exactly the same places. The coat was certainly mine, but the wooden button still puzzled me.

I called my mother while putting it on. She laughed when I described the problem. (3) ____ She had meant to tell me before I left for the club, but we had both been in a hurry. I suddenly remembered seeing the coat on the kitchen table beside her sewing box. At the time, I had paid no attention to what she was doing.

Walking home, I kept thinking about the button. A difference I had noticed immediately had almost made me ignore the stronger evidence inside the pocket. (4) ____ Next time, I would look a little further before deciding that an unexpected change meant something belonged to somebody else.

When I returned to the club room after helping outside, only one grey coat was hanging beside the door. It looked like mine, except that its top button was made of wood. Mine had a blue plastic button, or at least I thought it did. The room was empty, so there was nobody to ask. (1) I decided to leave it hanging there until its owner came back. That plan lasted only until I heard the rain against the windows. I needed to get home before it became heavier.

I checked the coat again, looking for something that a stranger would be unlikely to have. At first I found only an ordinary paper tissue. Then my fingers touched a rough edge hidden deeper in the lining. (2) It was the small square of red cloth inside the left pocket. I remembered sewing it there during a lesson after I had torn the pocket on a fence. The stitches were untidy in exactly the same places. The coat was certainly mine, but the wooden button still puzzled me.

I called my mother while putting it on. She laughed when I described the problem. (3) She had replaced the broken button earlier that morning. She had meant to tell me before I left for the club, but we had both been in a hurry. I suddenly remembered seeing the coat on the kitchen table beside her sewing box. At the time, I had paid no attention to what she was doing.

Walking home, I kept thinking about the button. A difference I had noticed immediately had almost made me ignore the stronger evidence inside the pocket.
